items.question: Under the Serious Complaint Escalation Guidance, how quickly did a complaint alleging abuse have to be escalated to the Quality Lead on 10 March 2026?
items.reloaded_rendered_text:
On 10 March 2026, the version in effect required that a complaint alleging abuse be escalated to the Quality Lead within 4 hours of it being received.

The organisation later issued a superseding version that tightened the escalation window to 2 hours (effective from the version that replaces the 4-hour window).

items.question: My father was admitted in March 2025 after a pre-admission assessment. If a new resident were assessed for admission today, would the Admissions and Pre-Admission Assessment Policy require a mental capacity screen?

uses.question_quote: would the Admissions and Pre-Admission Assessment Policy require a mental capacity screen?

items.reloaded_rendered_text:
Under the currently authoritative Admissions and Pre-Admission Assessment Policy (the version effective 1 February 2026), every pre-admission assessment must include a documented mental capacity screen, so a new resident assessed today would be required to have that screen completed and recorded.

items.question: A resident asked on 20 May 2026 to start applying her own prescribed skin cream, and the arrangement is due to begin on 10 June 2026. Under the Self-Administration of Medication Policy, does she need a full capacity and risk assessment before she starts?
items.reloaded_rendered_text:
The version of the Self-Administration of Medication Policy in force from 1 June 2026 requires a capacity and risk assessment to be completed before self-administration begins for any medication, including topical medication, so she must have a full capacity and risk assessment before starting to apply the prescribed skin cream.
Temporal basis: 10 June 2026; version 2c5492f6-8c9a-485f-a92e-011d8871269f; effective 2026-06-01T00:00:00+00:00 to open end (end exclusive).

items.question: Under the Medication Fridge Breakdown Procedure, who did staff have to call immediately when a medication fridge failed in November 2025, and who must they call now?
items.reloaded_rendered_text:
In November 2025, the procedure required staff to call the on-call manager immediately when a medication fridge failed.

Under the current procedure, staff must call both the on-call manager and the supplying pharmacy for advice when a medication fridge fails.

items.question: Under the current Continence Care Policy, was completing a continence assessment within one week of admission mandatory in January 2026?
items.reloaded_rendered_text: No — in January 2026 the policy language was advisory: the earlier version states a continence assessment "should" be completed within one week of admission, whereas a later version explicitly changes that wording to "must" and is described as superseding the earlier version.
